name: Question 2
problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=2x(t)-2y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=2x(t)-3y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[1,\text{ }2]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[2,\text{ }1]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options in the reasoning below. The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}\cdot {{field-1}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}\cdot {{field-2}}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y={{field-3}}
$$

and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{-2t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line. 

Since ${e}^{-2t}\to $ 
{{field-4}}
as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach 
{{field-5}} 
as $t\to \infty .$

Let's add the solutions to the phase space.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/e0446b7851fe0f0612d3db67de05188c0ed63af41ff1dfe2773158b2382fe722.png)

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y={{field-6}}
$$

and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line
